sections.h2: What kind of place is Framingham, Massachusetts?
sections.html:
Framingham is a city in Middlesex County and the MetroWest part of Greater Boston. It covers about 25 square miles of land and had 72,362 residents in the 2020 census, which made it the 14th most populous municipality in the state.

It was a town for more than 300 years. Framingham was incorporated in 1700, and before it changed status it was the largest town in Massachusetts by population. Voters approved a mayor and council charter in April 2017, and the city form of government began on January 1, 2018.

The area was home to the Nipmuc before English settlement, who lived along Farm Pond. The first European farm was started by John Stone in 1647, and Thomas Danforth later gathered more than 15,000 acres of grant land. The name comes from Danforth's hometown in England, with one letter dropped along the way.

sections.h2: How is Framingham laid out, and which areas do sellers hear about most?
sections.html:
Framingham is split into distinct business districts and villages, and a house in each one tends to attract a different kind of buyer. Local references describe three main commercial districts plus smaller village centers.

  • Golden Triangle: the retail and office district on the east side, bordered by Route 9, Route 30 and Speen Street. It grew from Shoppers World, opened in 1951, and TJX has its world headquarters at Route 30 and Speen Street.
  • Downtown and South Framingham: the commercial center that grew with the railroad in the 1880s. It held Dennison Manufacturing and the General Motors assembly plant until the late 1980s closures, then recovered partly through Brazilian and Hispanic immigration starting in the early 2000s.
  • West Framingham: centered on Route 9 with large office parks and the bulk of the city's apartment and condominium complexes.
  • Framingham Centre, Saxonville and Nobscot: older villages. The Framingham Centre Common Historic District is the physical and historic center, with Framingham State University beside it.

After World War II the town grew quickly, and much of the housing built in that period is split-level and ranch style. Sellers of those homes often deal with original kitchens, older baths and systems that have never been updated.

Framingham's economy comes mostly from retail and office complexes, with a scattering of small manufacturers and trade services. It is also known for the Framingham Heart Study and for the Dennison company, founded in 1844, which later merged into Avery Dennison.

Employers named in local references include TJX, Bose, Staples, Cumberland Farms, Genzyme and The MetroWest Daily News, spread between the Golden Triangle and the Route 9 industrial parks. Framingham State University and the Framingham campus of Massachusetts Bay Community College add education jobs and student housing demand.

For a seller, this mix means renters, commuters and employees of nearby office parks all show up as potential occupants. A house near Route 9 can carry both steady rental interest and heavy traffic noise.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit shape home values in Framingham?
sections.html:
Framingham sits roughly halfway between Boston and Worcester, and the road and rail links are a major reason people live here. The Massachusetts Turnpike (Interstate 90), Route 9, Route 30, Route 126 and Route 135 all cross the city.

Access pointWhat it offers
MBTA Framingham/Worcester LineCommuter rail to South Station and Back Bay; about 42 to 45 minutes to Back Bay
Logan ExpressDirect bus to Logan Airport from the Shoppers World property off Turnpike exit 13
MetroWest Regional Transit AuthorityRegional bus routes linking Framingham with nearby towns
Logan International AirportAbout 25 miles away

Downtown is split by the rail tracks and Waverly Street (Route 135). Homes within walking range of the station and the downtown streets draw commuters, while houses near the Turnpike and Route 9 interchanges draw buyers who want quick highway access.

Framingham Public Schools operates 14 public schools, including Framingham High School, three middle schools (Walsh, Fuller and Cameron) and nine elementary schools. The district's main offices are in the Fuller Administration Building on Flagg Drive.

The city also has a regional vocational high school, a regional charter school and several private schools. Buyers with children usually ask which elementary school serves a house, so have the school assignment answer ready from the district when you list or negotiate.

sections.h2: When are Framingham property tax installments due?
sections.html:
The City of Framingham bills property tax quarterly, and installments are due on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. Payments received after the due date accrue interest at 14 percent per year under G.L. c. 59, s. 57C, calculated from the day after the due date.

The city tries to mail bills at least 30 days before each due date. Not receiving a bill does not remove the obligation, so contact the Tax Collector if nothing arrives two or three weeks before a date. The Treasurer/Collector is at 150 Concord Street, Room 111, phone 508-532-5430.

If you sell in the middle of a billing quarter, the closing statement normally adjusts the current installment between seller and buyer. Ask the closing attorney to confirm which installments are paid and which are still open. You can read the city's explanation on its Important Tax Information page.

sections.h2: What does a Framingham smoke and carbon monoxide inspection involve?
sections.html:
Selling a one or two family home in Framingham requires a smoke and carbon monoxide detector inspection by the Fire Department before closing. The city asks you to apply and pay online, then call Fire Department Administration at 508-532-5930 to schedule the visit.

  • Allow at least three weeks between the inspection request and your closing date.
  • Inspections are generally held Monday to Friday, typically in the afternoon.
  • The house number must be on the structure itself, not on a door, at least 3 inches tall and visible from the nearest street.
  • Fire Headquarters is at 10 Loring Drive.

A failed inspection is a common reason a closing slips by a few days. Replacing old alarms before you apply is usually cheaper than a second visit. The city's inspection page links the requirements sheet.

sections.h2: What do Framingham sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Most Framingham sellers face the same few problems, and several come from the housing stock and the city's mix of neighborhoods.

  • Mid-century houses with dated systems that need work before a conventional buyer's lender will approve them.
  • Inherited homes where the owner lives out of state and has not cleared the contents.
  • Tenant-occupied homes and multi-family properties, especially near downtown and along Route 9.
  • Open tax installments or a closing date that has to fit around the three-week fire inspection lead time.

A cash buyer who purchases as-is can sidestep repair lists and showings, which matters most on inherited and tenant-occupied properties. You still need a clear title, an inspection certificate and tax adjustments at closing, so line those up early.

sections.h2: How do you decide between listing and a cash sale in Framingham?
sections.html:
Listing in Framingham makes sense when the house is in good shape and you can wait out showings, an appraisal and a buyer's financing. A cash sale makes sense when time, condition or occupancy is the bigger problem.

Compare the net amounts, not only the headline prices. A listing involves agent commission, repairs a lender may require and weeks of carrying costs such as tax installments and utilities. A direct sale removes several of those lines but usually comes at a lower number. Ask any buyer for their offer in writing, and ask the closing attorney what you would actually receive after the mortgage payoff and tax adjustments.

faqs.q: Is Framingham a town or a city?
faqs.a: Framingham is a city. Residents voted for a mayor and council charter in April 2017 and the city form took effect on January 1, 2018, after the municipality had been the largest town in Massachusetts.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and carbon monoxide inspection to sell in Framingham?
faqs.a: Yes. The Framingham Fire Department inspects residential smoke and carbon monoxide detectors for sales, and the city asks for at least three weeks of lead time before your closing date.

faqs.q: When are Framingham property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Installments are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. Late payments carry 14 percent annual interest under the cited state statute.
The MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line runs to South Station and Back Bay in Boston. Travel time to Back Bay is about 42 to 45 minutes.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Framingham house that has tenants?
faqs.a: You can sell it, and some cash buyers purchase tenant-occupied homes as-is. The lease stays in force, so ask the buyer how they handle the existing tenancy before you sign.
